clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: ROI-level t-tests (Bonferroni-Holm corrected) for group differences in z-scores; Spearman correlation (FDR corrected) between regional Z-scores and clinical severity scores (DSM, FTND) via partial correlation (excluding gender, head motion, Euler index).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Both IGD and TUD groups showed widespread cortical thinning, with individual-level heterogeneity, and distinct cortical thickness developmental trends were observed in the pericalcarine cortex between the two groups.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Both addiction groups exhibited widespread cortical thinning, particularly in regions such as the bilateral temporal pole and medial orbitofrontal cortex. The TUD group demonstrated a higher degree of individualization and limited spatial overlap compared to the IGD group. Opposite trends in CT changes were observed between the two groups in the bilateral pericalcarine cortex and pars triangularis. For positive extreme deviations, TUD accounted for 20.59% (14/68) of ROIs, while IGD accounted for 8.82% (6/68). For negative extreme deviations, TUD comprised 73.53% (50/68) of ROIs, compared to IGD's 42.65% (29/68). In the IGD group, DSM scores positively correlated with Z-scores in the left entorhinal cortex (r = 0.27, pFDR = 0.029), right lateral orbitofrontal cortex (r = 0.25, pFDR = 0.041), right parahippocampal gyrus (r = 0.25, pFDR = 0.004), and right frontal pole (r = 0.26, pFDR = 0.036). In the TUD group, FTND scores negatively correlated with Z-scores in the left lateral orbitofrontal cortex (r = -0.24, pFDR = 0.047), right medial orbitofrontal cortex (r = -0.38, pFDR = 0.001), right rostral anterior cingulate cortex (r = -0.28, pFDR = 0.016), right rostral middle frontal gyrus (r = -0.25, pFDR = 0.039), left superior parietal cortex (r = -0.29, pFDR = 0.015), and left superior temporal cortex (r = -0.27, pFDR = 0.023).

caa10_key_limitations.answer: ROI-wise analysis may lose local information; exclusion of other addictions by verbal inquiry only (lacking scale/biochemical data); GSP dataset lacks IGD/TUD diagnoses, potentially affecting normative modeling results; cross-sectional data limits brain development trajectory interpretation.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: Firstly, the analysis was performed on an ROI-wise rather than vertex-wise basis... Secondly, this study only excluded participants with other types of addiction through verbal inquiry... Thirdly, the GSP dataset does not provide diagnoses for IGD and TUD... Lastly, the trajectory of brain development was based on the cross-sectional data

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study combined group-level and individualized analyses of deviations using normative modeling to identify individual differences. It used 10-fold cross-validation for unbiased estimation and a fixed statistical significance threshold (z=±2.6) for extreme deviations to simplify comparisons. Analyses were performed using Python software, version 3.8.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Age and education level matching was performed on the groups using the non-parametric nearest neighbor matching procedure provided by the MatchIt package in R.
